text:
ajay: quick heads-up — ran an nsys trace on canary after the quant+batch tuning deploy (commit `b6f3c9`). seeing layer-norm-ish kernel dominating time now (was tiny before). trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/2759991234

ajay: top kernels from the nsys summary:
```
> linalg_layer_norm_fwd         42.1%  0.42s
> attn_matmul_qk                18.3%  0.18s
> kv_cache_prefetch             10.2%  0.10s
> softmax                       7.6%   0.076s
```

ajay: that 42% is new — before deploy layer_norm was ~6-8% on same workload. digging in.

lisa: @ajay wow, huge. any diffs in input shapes or padding? could quant fusion produce a different codepath? :thinking_face:

sam: pinging the batch heuristic change: we lowered the dynamic batching threshold to 8 tokens per request last week. more small batches could kill occupancy. can you correlate sample sizes?

ajay: good call. sample distribution shifted: median seq len same, but median batch size dropped 1.8 -> 1.1 after the tuning (more singletons). I think we moved some requests off the prefix cache so layernorm runs per token more often.

ryan: can you dump the kernel launch params? want to see grid/block and shared mem usage for that kernel. small launches -> SM underutilization.

ajay: pasted a couple launches from the trace (nsys raw):
```
linalg_layer_norm_fwd kernelLaunch: grid=(128,1,1) block=(128,1,1) shared=512 bytes
prev: grid=(2048,1,1) block=(256,1,1) shared=2048 bytes
```

ajay: small grid/block now. occupancy computed at ~12% for most frames. previous runs were ~58%.

sam: OK that's the smoking gun for SM util. Two hypotheses: (1) quant fusion changed tiling and made per-row work smaller, (2) batching heuristic creating lots of 1-element batches.

lisa: also check KV cache path — if prefix cache miss forces recompute of residuals each time, layernorm may be called extra. any increases in `kv_cache_prefetch` or `kv_read` counts?

ajay: kv_cache_prefetch increased ~3x in the trace, matches idea. I can repro in a small micro-bench with `--batch-override 16` vs `1`.

ryan: run perfetto with `--timeline` and capture occupancy heatmap. also try forcing the old kernel selection with env `RW_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` to see if CPU-side selection is the issue.

ajay: running both now. quick local numbers: batch=16 -> layer_norm 6.8%, batch=1 -> 40.5% (same shape as canary). saving traces to s3 `s3://perf-debug/2759991234/`.

deploy-bot: deployment b6f3c9 completed to canary at 2026-03-18T15:12:02Z

sam: plan: 1) reproduce with small bench 2) try kernel selector env toggle 3) if selector is fine, roll back batching tweak or increase threshold 4) follow-up: add micro-bench to CI to catch this regress (check layernorm % and occupancy).

ajay: agreed. i'll push the micro-bench PR and attach traces + perfetto links. will update thread with results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
